Alert · what 24 messages used to look like, and what they look like now

Bindery drew every message as a tinted box: a coloured ground, a coloured border, and coloured body text. The system draws an alert as a raised surface with a coloured title — elevation is tone, and colour is spent on the one word that carries the meaning rather than on the whole region. This is the change, at real size, in Bindery's own tokens.

The banner — a new flush placement, not a new component

Two places put a message edge-to-edge under a panel header. A boxed alert with a radius floating inside a flush panel fights the header's rhythm, so flush keeps the raised ground and trades the radius for a boundary at the edge it meets.

After

normalize · page · segment · embed

The trade being made. The tinted version is louder, and on a screen holding one message that is not a fault. It stops working when a screen holds several — Trust and Admin each show three or four at once — because a wall of coloured grounds has no hierarchy left to spend. Colour on the title alone keeps the tone legible and lets the eye find which message is the urgent one.
